item.title: Bitcoin verstehen – Episode 338 - Bitcoin wird von allen Seiten angegriffen: Ledger-Attacke, Binance-Hack & was du jetzt tun kannst. Mit Chris (Seedor & Bitsurance)
item.description:
🔐 Wir veranstalten Live-Masterclasses zur Bitcoin-Aufbewahrung: Von der Ersteinrichtung einer Hardwarewallet bis zu fortgeschrittenen Themen wie optionaler Passphrase und Multisig. Trag dich in die Warteliste ein und erfahre als Erstes, wann es losgeht.


In dieser Folge sprechen wir mit Chris von Bitsurance und Seedor über zwei Angriffe, die gerade die Bitcoin-Welt beschäftigen: den Lieferkettenangriff auf Ledger und den Hack bei Binance. Wir klären, was bei Ledger passiert ist, wie die Implantate funktionieren und woran du ein manipuliertes Gerät erkennst. Dazu geht es um Binance, um die Frage, warum Börsen so angreifbar sind, und darum, ob Bitcoin gerade angegriffen wird. Am Ende gibt Chris drei Schritte mit, die du in den nächsten Wochen angehen kannst.



🔗 LINKS ZUR FOLGE


▪ Unsere letzte Folge mit Chris zum Coldcard-Hack

▪ Übersicht manipulierter Ledger-Geräte

▪ Multisig-Tutorial mit mehreren Hardwarewallets

▪ Artikel zu Trezor-Vorfall

▪ Artikel zu Binance


📋 TIMESTAMPS


(00:00:00) Einleitung

(00:01:34) Was ist beim Ledger-Hack passiert?

(00:11:55) Attacke auf die Lieferkette

(00:14:40) Worauf sollte man selbst achten?

(00:36:20) Übersicht zum Binance-Hack

(00:43:20) Was bedeutet das für Bitcoin?

item.title: einemillionsatoshi - der Bitcoin Podcast – Bitcoin und Beziehung: Warum Überzeugen selten funktioniert
item.description:
Deine Begeisterung für Bitcoin ist riesig, aber zu Hause stößt du auf Granit? In dieser Folge von "einemillionsatoshi" erfährst du, wie du das Thema Bitcoin in deine Beziehung bringst, ohne einen Familienstreit auszulösen. item.title: Der Relai Bitcoin Podcast – Zwei Freunde, eine Mission: Bitcoin verständlich machen, Manuel & Jonas von Bitcoin verstehen | Relai Bitcoin Podcast #131
item.description:
Manuel & Jonas sind die Hosts vom beliebten Podcast, Bitcoin verstehen. Darin bringen sie mit spannenden Videos, Tutorials, sowie Interviews dem Zuschauer die Grundlagen und Ideen hinter Bitcoin näher.

Im Gespräch mit Relai-CEO Julian Liniger sprechen die beiden über ihre Erfrahrung als Podcast Hosts, weshalb sie sich dazu entschieden haben den Podcast zu lancieren, wie sie Anfängern Bitcoin näherbringen, und was als Nächstes ansteht.

Folge Bitcoin verstehen auf X: https://x.com/BTCVerstehenPod

Oder abonniere den Podcast hier: https://bitcoinverstehen.info/

—

⏱ Kapitel:

00:00 - Intro und Vorstellung

02:30 - Wie Manuel und Jonas sich kennengelernt haben

03:45 - Die Entstehung von Bitcoin verstehen

12:50 - Bitcoin erklären vor allem als digitales Gold

19:32 - Der Unterscheid mit ETFs und echten Bitcoin

25:10 - Möglichkeiten, das Vertrauen bei Verwahrenden zu reduzieren

item.title: Dein Weg zu Bitcoin – Michael Saylor im Orange Jacket – Abu über Bitcoin & Mut im Unternehmertum – Dein Weg zu Bitcoin
item.description:
Abu habe ich vor zwei Jahren im Bitcoin-Hotel in Plochingen kennengelernt, und seitdem schaue ich ihm fasziniert zu. Er hat mit BitArt eine der ersten Bitcoin-Kunstgalerien Europas gegründet, mit 21Million Fashion ein Bitcoin-Modelabel aufgebaut und in Abu Dhabi Michael Saylor sein eigenes Orange Jacket überreicht. Einen Plan dafür gab es nie. Was es immer gab, war eine Vision und den Mut, einfach loszugehen.Was passiert, wenn du einem Traum folgst, für den es keinen Bauplan gibt?👉 Wie Abu nach einem Jahr Vorarbeit 15 Sekunden mit Michael Saylor bekam und warum die Jacke auf Anhieb passte👉 Warum Proof of Work für ihn auch Handwerk, Stoffe und echte Qualität beschreibt👉 Was ein Cappuccino 2017 in Sats gekostet hat und was heute👉 Wie Hameln Bitcoin in die Stadt bringen will, bis hin zu einer Bibliothek, beheizt mit Mining-Abwärme👉 Warum Scheitern kein Scheitern istMich hat in diesem Gespräch vor allem eins berührt: Abu redet nicht über Erfolg, sondern über den Weg dorthin. Über schlechte Tage, an denen er alles hinschmeißen will. Über Samen, die er streut, ohne zu wissen, welcher aufgeht.„Vision ohne Aktion ist Halluzination.“ – Abu

🔗 LinksAbu: https://www.instagram.com/abullishonbitcoin/21 Million Fashion: https://www.21million-fashion.com/Weser-Wirtschaftsforum: https://wwforum.org/Zukunftsdialog Hameln: 10. Juni 2027✨ Mein Ziel: Bitcoin verständlich machen – mit Geschichten, die zeigen, dass die ersten Schritte nicht groß sein müssen.👍 Gefällt dir die Folge? item.title: Sound Money Bitcoin Podcast – #350 Die Akte Lagarde: Mehr Geld, mehr Schulden, weniger wert
item.description:
Christine Lagarde verlässt die EZB am 7. Februar 2027, fast neun Monate vor dem regulären Ende ihrer Amtszeit, und das bei einer Inflation von 3,8 Prozent im Euroraum.


Zeit für eine Abrechnung: Wir schauen, wer die Juristin ohne geldpolitische Ausbildung eigentlich ist und wie sie an die Spitze der zweitwichtigsten Notenbank der Welt kam. Wir vergleichen ihre Amtszeit mit denen ihrer Vorgänger Trichet und Draghi und zeigen, warum ausgerechnet unter „Whatever it takes“-Draghi die Kaufkraft besser erhalten blieb.


Dazu geht es um ihren Fehlstart in der Corona-Krise, die als „vorübergehend“ verharmloste Inflation und neue Instrumente wie PEPP und TPI, mit denen die EZB heute gezielt einzelne Staaten stützen kann.


In Zahlen: Unter Lagarde hat der Euro rund 21,5 Prozent seiner Kaufkraft verloren, aus 100 Euro wurden real 78,50 Euro. Außerdem ordnen wir ein, warum der Zeitpunkt ihres Abgangs kurz vor der französischen Präsidentschaftswahl kein Zufall ist und was das über die Unabhängigkeit der Notenbank aussagt. Am Ende gibt es ein ehrliches Arbeitszeugnis und meine Einschätzung, was das für dein Erspartes, für Aktien, Gold und Bitcoin bedeutet.

item.title: The Bitcoin Matrix – Aaron Siri: The One Product You Can't Sue in America
item.description:
"People say 'I believe in vaccines.' Nobody says that about seatbelts."

Aaron Siri is the managing partner of Siri & Glimstad and, by most measures, the most consequential vaccine litigator in America. He's the attorney behind the famous nine-hour deposition of Dr. Stanley Plotkin — the man they call the godfather of vaccines — lead counsel for the Informed Consent Action Network (ICAN), a 2025 Senate witness, and a central legal figure in the RFK-era reshaping of federal vaccine policy. His new book is Vaccines, Amen: The Religion of Vaccines — in his words, "a cross-examination in book form."

This one steps outside the show's usual lane, and I want to be upfront: this is not medical advice, I'm not a doctor, and everything Aaron argues here is his own case — where it's contested by public-health bodies, treat it as one side of an open debate. What ties it to this show is the question we always ask: how do you know what's real when you're not allowed to check? From there we go deep — how a custody case led to the legendary Plotkin deposition; the Hepatitis B shot Aaron says was licensed on a trial of 147 kids, five days of monitoring, and no control group; the 1986 law he calls "the original sin" that handed vaccine makers liability immunity; the Ford Pinto and what punitive damages actually do; informed consent versus the right to refuse; whether vaccines really stop transmission; and the measles-mortality data he argues almost no one talks about. A conversation about evidence, incentives, and who gets to audit the people in charge.

Subscribe so you never miss an episode.

item.title: Bitcoin & Beyond | Der New-Finance-Podcast – Sparkassen-Digitalminister: Wir haben „keine Angst“ vor Trade Republic
item.description:
Über die Sparkassen mit ihren 50 Millionen Kunden gibt es viele Klischees: Ein bisschen langweilig, altbacken und teuer seien sie, heißt es. Joachim Schmalzl mag keines dieser Vorurteile bestätigen – schon qua Job nicht: Er ist so etwas wie der Digitalminister der Sparkassen. Im Podcast sprechen wir mit ihm darüber,

  • mit welchem neuen Börsen-Angebot die Sparkassen jetzt Trade Republic und Co. kontern,
  • wieso sie beim Altersvorsorgedepot Neobroker unterbieten (und sie trotzdem auch ein teures Produkt anbieten),
  • warum Schmalzl kein Problem darin sieht, dass die Sparkassen beim Tagesgeld knausern
  • und wieso Sparkassen-Kunden jetzt auch Kryptowährungen kaufen können, obwohl Schmalzl rein gar nichts davon hält.

Disclaimer: Dieser Podcast ist keine Anlageberatung, sondern dient lediglich der Information und Unterhaltung. Die Hosts oder der Verlag übernehmen keine Haftung für Anlageentscheidungen, die ihr aufgrund der im Podcast gehörten Informationen trefft.

Die Folge basiert auf Kapitel 21 meines Buchs. Atmosphäre und Dialoge wurden für den Podcast dramaturgisch erweitert.


In dieser Folge:

• Entwickleraktivität prüfen, ohne Commit-Zahlen mit Qualität zu verwechseln.

• Aktive Adressen, Menschen und Bots auseinanderhalten.

• Nutzung und möglichen Tokenwert getrennt betrachten.

• Tokenomics und Unlocks einordnen, ohne sichere Kursprognosen.

• Primärquellen kritisch lesen und Werbedruck erkennen.

• Warum Kursverluste und Vesting keine pauschalen Steuerregeln erlauben.

item.title: Swan Signal Live - A Bitcoin Show – John Haar Returns: Why the Fed Must Talk Tough While It Inflates
item.description:
• John reads Warsh's Jackson Hole speech as a nothing burger for Bitcoiners: a Fed chair must talk tough on inflation because signaling anything else would send inflation expectations and yields higher, while the long-run path of financial repression stays the same
  • Warsh reported that 54% of PCE basket components rose more than 3% over the past year, called 4.1% unemployment full employment, and framed inflation as squarely the Fed's problem to solve
  • Markets read the speech as hawkish anyway: the two-year yield rose about 12 basis points while gold and Bitcoin each gave back roughly 3.5%
  • On last week's expanded Treasury buybacks, John points to two signals: a 30-year yield near 5.3% is clearly bothering policymakers, and the Fed has never meaningfully reduced its holdings of 10-year-plus Treasuries even during quantitative tightening, evidence that natural buyers of long-dated government paper are scarce
  • The hosts revisit the shallowest bear market thesis they developed together on this show: a roughly 52% drawdown against 77% to 90%-plus in prior cycles, with the June low of $58,000 sitting just below the 200-week moving average before price rocketed back through it
  • John explains why he believes the June low will hold, while framing the 50-week moving average near $82,000 as the level the market is watching to declare a new bull market
  • Glassnode data shows 1.05 million Bitcoin of long-term holder supply with a cost basis between $83,000 and $86,000, the first heavy resistance shelf above spot, and the hosts discuss how cost basis shapes market psychology
  • The debasement trade is back in ETF volumes, with GLD and IBIT both in the top ten most traded funds, and the Bitcoin-to-gold ratio breaking its year-long downtrend after gold's 2025 outperformance
  • Bitcoin's long correlation with software stocks broke down in June, and John argues it was always the wrong frame, a point Lyn Alden's Wall Street Journal essay makes at length: Bitcoin is a protocol of value, not another technology stock
  • A broad Treasury ETF has returned roughly negative 18% after inflation over fifteen years while the supply of government debt keeps expanding, the picture John says is quietly ending the era of Treasuries as the world's default store of value

item.title: Bitcoin, Fiat & Rock'n'Roll – Banks Become Custodians, Crypto Firms Become Banks | Monthly Briefing
item.description:
Moving securities and money onto blockchains leaves familiar questions about ownership, custody and redemption. In BFRR’s October 2026 news review, co-hosts Dr. Michael Blaschke and Stefan Grasmann examine how banks, crypto firms and regulators are handling those obligations.

The SEC’s innovation exemption for tokenized US stocks provides one test. The hosts explore third-party tokenization, issuer objections and US securities industry group SIFMA’s concerns about shareholder rights. In Europe, Boerse Stuttgart Group’s trading and settlement license provides the regulatory basis for Seturion, while ESMA asks how tokenized collateral would perform if a clearing member defaults.


Stablecoins, Tokenization, Custody, MiCA, GENIUS, JPMorgan

item.title: bitcoin ist - Wissen statt FOMO – 24) ... Energie mit zwei Leben
item.description:
Bitcoin und Energieverbrauch werden oft in einem negativen Zusammenhang genannt. Diese Folge zeigt ein differenzierteres Bild: warum Bitcoin-Mining Stromnetze stabilisieren kann, wie aus Abwärme ein zweiter Wertschöpfungskreislauf entsteht, und wo die Grenzen dieser Entwicklung aktuell noch liegen.

Themen in dieser Folge:

  • Wie sich der Anteil nachhaltiger Energien beim Bitcoin-Mining seit 2022 entwickelt hat
  • Warum der Ausbau von Wind- und Solarenergie ein Netzstabilitätsproblem mit sich bringt
  • Wie Bitcoin-Miner als flexible Last genutzt werden können, um Lastspitzen abzupuffern
  • Warum jede Kilowattstunde beim Mining "zwei Leben" bekommt: Bitcoin-Belohnung und nutzbare Wärme
  • Drei Unternehmen, die das bereits umsetzen: Terahash, 21energy und Power2Bit


Die Anfangs erwähnte Studie der Cambridge University

https://www.jbs.cam.ac.uk/2025/cambridge-study-sustainable-energy-rising-in-bitcoin-mining/


Erwähnte Unternehmen:

  • Terahash – Bitcoin-Mining Infrastruktur für Unternehmen
  • 21energy – Bitcoin-Heizungen für Privathaushalte und Kleingewerbe
  • Power2Bit – flexible, klimaneutrale Rechenzentren und kommunale Wärmeplanung


Hinweis: Die genannten Prozentzahlen zum Energiemix variieren je nach Berechnungsmethode (konservativer Netzmix vs. direkte Unternehmensmeldungen) und waren zum Zeitpunkt der Aufnahme aktuell.

]]>

item.title: Bitcoin Today Recast – Strategy’s $6.5 Billion Convertible Debt Wall: What Happens by 2029? | Bitcoin, MSTR & Corporate Debt Risk | Nov. 3, 2026
item.description:
Darkside does the math Michael Saylor leaves out: Strategy owes $1 billion in September 2027 if MSTR closes below $183, $2 billion in March 2028 below $433, and $3.5 billion more by 2029, while roughly $1 billion every five weeks goes into buying back STRC. Tomer Strolight shows how Grok's reverse-split error made Strive (ASST) look up 200 percent while it fell 83 percent, and Fred Krueger notes ASST is down about 80 percent since Matt Cole took over. TC explains why a permissionless purchase from an Indian pharmacy during COVID mattered more than price, and Jethro, Scott Wolfe, and Pursuing Freedom preview El Salvador's Bitcoin month, with 1,400 merchants accepting Bitcoin and Historico at the National Palace. item.title: The Bitcoin Layer – The Fed Will Have To Print Bigger This Time
item.description: <![CDATA[In this episode, Nik lays out three money market metrics he watches as a former repo and treasury bill trader, and why they suggest the Fed may be closer to another round of QE than anyone wants to admit. He starts with SOFR creeping back above IORB, a spread now at its widest since tax day, and the month end and year end dates he is watching next. He then covers why more than $7 trillion in T-bills has to be funded by a cash market that cannot grow to meet it, and why bank reserves at 9% of GDP sit near the levels that preceded the 2019 repo crisis.]]>

item.title: Bitcoiners - Live From Bitcoin Beach – Moving Your Bitcoin Business to El Salvador? What to Know About Banks, Residency and Self-Custody | Carlos Gil of ECIJA
item.description:
Before anyone was buying property in El Salvador with Bitcoin, Mike called a lawyer to ask whether giving Bitcoin away in El Zonte could put him in jail.

You’ve heard the country made Bitcoin legal tender. What you haven’t heard is what that did to one law office, one land deal and one very stubborn banking system.

That lawyer is Carlos Gil, partner at the Salvadoran office of ECIJA, an international law firm. He’d never heard of Bitcoin when Mike called around 2011 or 2012. He read the paper, and a few months later he was on board.

Then came the day Bukele announced legal tender. Carlos’s phone rang nonstop the next morning with international clients asking about taxes, capital gains and how to keep their books. By 2022 he was at a Bitcoin conference where strangers bought him lunch just for being Salvadoran.

Then Mike bought land. The closing took six hours because QR codes on the Bitcoin Beach wallet expired every minute and the seller’s brand-new custodial account couldn’t hold the full price. Carlos explains what self custody turns that into, and why a wire from the U.S. still gets flagged while Bitcoin doesn’t.

Through all of it, the banks were the slow part. Carlos tells foreign clients to keep Bitcoin off their corporate documents because El Salvador banks wouldn’t open accounts for Bitcoin companies, and his first one waited three months. Here’s where it gets strange. Banks from Colombia, Honduras and Guatemala are now the ones getting licenses, and a bank president who once turned people away called Mike a year ago asking for a favor.

Where that leaves the El Salvador economy today, in Carlos’s words, is a sandbox where international chains and El Salvador real estate companies come to test the technology, while a bank officer still can’t process a man who held Bitcoin for 15 years and wants to retire in La Libertad.

That same financial innovation grew his firm from two people to 64 lawyers and gave a Salvadoran born in the ’80s something new. For the first time, his country was known for something good!

Whether you’re moving to El Salvador to set up a company or just want to know if the legal side holds up, listen before you decide. The lawyer’s answer starts with “it depends.”


—Bitcoin Beach Team

item.itunes:summary:
Before anyone was buying property in El Salvador with Bitcoin, Mike called a lawyer to ask whether giving Bitcoin away in El Zonte could put him in jail.

You’ve heard the country made Bitcoin legal tender. What you haven’t heard is what that did to one law office, one land deal and one very stubborn banking system.

That lawyer is Carlos Gil, partner at the Salvadoran office of ECIJA, an international law firm. He’d never heard of Bitcoin when Mike called around 2011 or 2012. He read the paper, and a few months later he was on board.

Then came the day Bukele announced legal tender. Carlos’s phone rang nonstop the next morning with international clients asking about taxes, capital gains and how to keep their books. By 2022 he was at a Bitcoin conference where strangers bought him lunch just for being Salvadoran.

Then Mike bought land. The closing took six hours because QR codes on the Bitcoin Beach wallet expired every minute and the seller’s brand-new custodial account couldn’t hold the full price. Carlos explains what self custody turns that into, and why a wire from the U.S. still gets flagged while Bitcoin doesn’t.

Through all of it, the banks were the slow part. Carlos tells foreign clients to keep Bitcoin off their corporate documents because El Salvador banks wouldn’t open accounts for Bitcoin companies, and his first one waited three months. Here’s where it gets strange. Banks from Colombia, Honduras and Guatemala are now the ones getting licenses, and a bank president who once turned people away called Mike a year ago asking for a favor.

Where that leaves the El Salvador economy today, in Carlos’s words, is a sandbox where international chains and El Salvador real estate companies come to test the technology, while a bank officer still can’t process a man who held Bitcoin for 15 years and wants to retire in La Libertad.

That same financial innovation grew his firm from two people to 64 lawyers and gave a Salvadoran born in the ’80s something new. For the first time, his country was known for something good!

Whether you’re moving to El Salvador to set up a company or just want to know if the legal side holds up, listen before you decide. The lawyer’s answer starts with “it depends.”


—Bitcoin Beach Team

item.title: The Café Bitcoin Podcast – The Finale: Liquid's 4,000 Bitcoin, the Caching Bug, and 50 Days for Freedom Wrapped
item.description:
• The last day. Brady opened with the count, 37 shows in 50 days, and the campaign's frame: political independence 250 years ago, monetary independence now. Yan Pritzker, Frank Corva, Suze and Alec on stage; Unseen Finance returned at the end.
  • The Liquid hack, plainly. On Sunday somebody sent 4,000 L-BTC to SideSwap's peg-out and the Liquid Federation paid out real Bitcoin. The L-BTC had been created from nothing. Blockstream paused the sidechain and 3,400 Bitcoin came back Monday.
  • ⭐ Yan on what broke: a caching bug, not anyone's keys. "The only two hard problems in computer science are naming and cache invalidation." Two transactions shared one cache key, so validators mistook a fake for one already checked.
  • Why it is not Bitcoin. Yan: Liquid is an 11-of-15 federation of companies with its own database and rules. "This is a separate thing, this is not Bitcoin itself." Lightning is built on Bitcoin script; Liquid is not.
  • ⭐ Frank on the 15%. The hackers returned 85% and kept about 600 Bitcoin. His question: will anyone be made whole, and if they keep it, "they're surely not white hats." A Bitcoin Policy Institute lawyer offered to talk.
  • Yan's verdict on the hat color: gray. Taking everything to beat a black hat is arguable. Keeping a cut is not. "You don't just return a wallet and take a bunch of stuff out of it."
  • Suze's question: Bitcoiners are ruthless about added trust assumptions, so why did Liquid get a pass? "Were we discerning enough?" Leave the base layer and you take on another code base and another set of failure points.
  • ⭐ Yan on open source in the AI era: it stays because every open project gets red-teamed by the whole internet. Closed systems get hacked too, "we just don't hear about them." The base chain is "the ultimate boss" nobody has beaten.
  • Yan's bank numbers, read live from the Identity Theft Resource Center: 3,332 reported data compromises in 2025 affecting 280 million people, 739 of them in financial services. "Bank-grade security" is not a standard anyone actually meets.
  • ⭐ Frank's hard question: must the layers be as bulletproof as Bitcoin? Yan: nothing is, and the only path is slow growth. Bitcoin was attacked at $1, then $10,000, then a billion. Early adopters carry the risk.
  • Yan's rocket-ship rule. Bitcoin Core engineering is closer to launching a spacecraft than shipping web software. "Years of careful review, study, simulations on other chains." Test new tech on other coins for two years first.
  • Suze asked whether ossification risks losing the skills to change Bitcoin in 50 years. Frank and Yan: no. Ossification is no new features, not no developers, and AI has widened who can work on cryptography and game theory.
  • Yan on open-weight versus hosted AI: the same debate as open source versus closed, and open source won the internet. His advice to companies: externalize memory, skills and harness so you can swap models. Swan built its own.
  • Unseen Finance returned with a proposal: these incidents are a credibility problem for the services on top of Bitcoin, not for Bitcoin. His fix, borrowed from banking: a self-regulatory body plus an insurance pool that service providers pay into.
  • Brady's tally at the close: Cory, Yan, Steve, Alec, Isaiah, Matt and Brandon from Swan; Larry Lepard three times; Parker Lewis, Daniel Batten, Tom and Callum, Guy Swann, Ryan MacLeod, Alana, Bob Burnett, Roxana. Suze made 35 of 37.
  • The close. "We have the tools, we have the knowledge, we have the culture, we have the determination." The half-price buy fee ends today; limit orders placed today keep it. Yan's last word: take security seriously, "go play with AI."
    • ]]>

item.title: The Bitcoin Infinity Show – A Master’s Degree in Bitcoin with Kristyna Mazankova | Bitcoin Infinity Show #227
item.description:
Kristyna Mazankova joins the Bitcoin Infinity Show to talk about launching the Master in Bitcoin at Hesperides University, the world’s first English-language master’s program dedicated entirely to Bitcoin, and why she insists it take no government money. She and Knut dig into what’s broken in state-funded higher education, why Bitcoin companies struggle to hire people who truly understand Bitcoin, and how the program aims to shape builders and entrepreneurs rather than employees. Along the way they cover her start at Trezor, the Czech roots of Slush Pool and Bitcoin mining pools, KYC versus KYC-free ways to stack sats, self-custody, and the hidden risks of Bitcoin treasury stocks and ETFs.

🗞️ Join 14,000 subscribers who get our free weekly newsletter: https://www.thebitcoinway.com/resources/newsletter?utm_source=tbw&utm_medium=fountain&utm_campaign=bitcoin-banter&utm_content=desc

=========================

Two Bitcoin hardware wallet makers, Keystone and Foundation, were hit by data breaches within 10 days of each other. Customers' names, home addresses and phone numbers leaked, and convincing phishing emails followed. Michael, Tony and Katie explain why the customer database was the weak point, and what to do before you order your next device.

Then Apple's own privacy report says the average app has six trackers, and Tony makes his case for a privacy phone. Plus unauthorised AI agents inside US bank accounts, France's government weighing up blocking social media during the protests, and new powers for HMRC to take money straight from UK bank accounts.

And one tech investor's latest Bitcoin call earns him Donkey of the Week.

=========================

item.description:
Democrats won both chambers in a historic midterm wave. Mike Katz and Justin Slaughter on what that means for the Clarity Act, DeFi and crypto's next 2 years.

========================================================

Thank you to our sponsor!

  • Put your crypto to work with Nexo: earn daily interest or borrow funds against your assets on one platform trusted by more than 10 million clients.

Quick favor: We’re deciding what Unchained does next; new shows, stream times, what’s worth paying for.

Our ⁠⁠listener survey⁠⁠ takes five minutes, it’s anonymous, and I read the write-in answers myself. Everyone who finishes it gets a free month of Premium, Unchained or Bits + Bips, your pick. Open through Sunday, November 8.

— Laura

========================================================

Democrats swept both chambers of Congress in the midterms, winning the popular vote by 13 points, according to Justin Slaughter. For an industry still waiting on a market structure law, the question is what a Democratic Congress now does with crypto.

Slaughter, Senior Advisor at Paradigm and Board Member of the Long-Term Stock Exchange, and Mike Katz, Partner of Leading Frontier Tech at Manatt, join Laura Shin to explain why the Clarity Act looks dead, what a House Financial Services market structure bill may contain, whether SEC and CFTC rules survive, and how Elizabeth Warren at Senate Banking could steer oversight of the Trump family's crypto deals.

They also cover the banks' pressure on Genius Act rulemaking, a Texas data center pause and what it means for Bitcoin miners, and why Fairshake spending $56 million against Sherrod Brown, who still won, may force crypto to rethink its political strategy before 2028.

item.title: Stephan Livera Podcast – Why Heat-Reuse Mining Gets Stronger Every Halving | Alex Busarov SLP787
item.description:
Alex Busarov, founder of Heatbit, argues that water heating, not space heating, makes home Bitcoin mining add up. His new Bitwater element replaces a water heater’s lower heating element, mines all year, and he says it adds no extra energy cost because the heat is used anyway.

Stephan presses him on the two-to-three-year payback claim, the hashrate and price assumptions behind it, a plan to give devices away for free while Heatbit keeps the hashrate, decentralization risk, limescale and maintenance, the Bitair purifier, and why halvings strengthen the case for heat reuse.

00:00 — Intro

00:35 — From a Loud S9 to Heatbit

02:04 — ROI, Ideology or Gift?

04:03 — Bitair: $179 Purifier, Not ROI

05:31 — Solo Pool by Default, Noise Modes

07:04 — Bitwater Price and Plumbing Value

08:49 — The 2–3 Year Payback Claim

09:50 — Free Devices, Heatbit Keeps the Hash

12:18 — Assumptions: Flat Price, Flat Hashrate

13:52 — Element Lifetime and Limescale Failure

14:59 — B2B Installers and Unwitting Miners

17:01 — Water Heating vs the Mining Network

17:59 — Decentralization and Miners Who Hold

20:31 — Efficiency: BM1370 and “Zero Incremental”

22:11 — Maintenance, Leaks and Limescale

24:55 — Should Every Heating Element Mine?

26:29 — Becoming a Miner With No Power Bill

27:29 — Utilization: The Heat-Reuse Variable

30:08 — Maxi, Trio and Canvas Space Heaters

32:43 — Space Heaters Pay Back Slower

34:58 — Halvings as Heat Reuse’s Tailwind


Show links

  • Alex Busarov on X: https://x.com/alex_heatbit
  • Heatbit on X: https://x.com/heatbit_com
  • Heatbit: https://heatbit.com/
]]>

item.title: BITCOIN & ALTCOINS – Bitcoin & Altcoins: Wie geht es nach dem Oktober-Dämpfer weiter?
item.description:
Viele Anleger hatten auf einen starken Oktober gehofft. Stattdessen verlor Bitcoin im Monatsverlauf mehr als 7 Prozent. Zur schwachen Stimmung trugen neben dem Cyberangriff auf Binance auch enttäuschende Nachrichten zu KI-Investitionen und den Plänen großer Tech-Konzerne wie Microsoft, Amazon und Intel bei. Was steckt hinter diesen Entwicklungen, welchen Einfluss könnten die Midterms auf die Märkte haben und wie ist die aktuelle Stimmung bei Bitcoin und Altcoins einzuschätzen? Über diese Fragen spricht Oliver Michel von tokentus Investment AG in diesem Interview.

Hinweis: Die im Podcast besprochenen Coins und Token stellen keine spezifischen Kauf- oder Anlageempfehlungen dar. Die Moderatoren oder der Verlag haften nicht für etwaige Verluste, die aufgrund der Umsetzung der im Podcast diskutierten Gedanken oder Ideen entstehen.

Das Gespräch wurde am 03.11.2026 an der Frankfurter Börse aufgezeichnet.

Tägliche Informationen gefällig? Dann ab zu „Krypto-Insights“ – dem Telegram-Kanal von Oliver Michel und Johanna Krämer. Weitere Infos unter www.krypto-insights.de

item.title: THE Bitcoin Podcast – Bitcoin’s Disbelief Rally: Who Is Left to Sell? | James Check & Michael Sullivan
item.description:
Who is left to sell Bitcoin?

James Check (Checkmate) and Michael Sullivan are back for round two after Peak Apathy. We put Check’s on-chain analysis alongside Michael’s language-based sentiment research to explore the gap between Bitcoin’s recovering price and the crowd’s lingering disbelief.

Check explains his seller-exhaustion thesis and why a calendar is no substitute for studying how holders behave. Michael breaks down excitement, desire, fear and anger—and why hoping for a higher price is not the same as buying Bitcoin.

We also discuss coin age and spending behavior, DCA versus emotional buying, how to measure Bitcoin’s returns, and why quieter Bitcoiners may simply be busy building businesses and raising families. Then we zoom out to adoption “one funeral at a time,” shifting narratives, AI, scarcity, and the history embedded in Bitcoin’s UTXO set.

Both guests remain bullish, but their thesis is not a guarantee: Check allows for another selloff, and Michael explicitly separates his long-term conviction from the next two weeks.

Recorded October 19, 2026.

item.title: The "What is Money?" Show – From Pain and Addiction to Finding Bitcoin /w Andrew Sanchez
item.description:
Andrew Sanchez tells a story that runs from childhood dysfunction and ADHD medication to chronic pain, addiction, homelessness, and his journey from anti capitalist to anarcho capitalist.

He shares how radical honesty and a judge's mercy opened the door to mental health court, how a four leaf clover landed at his feet the day his record was cleared, and how typing what is money into YouTube led him to the show and to Bitcoin. They also cover the cobra effect, Rene Girard and mimetic desire, the difference between logic and reason, a priori versus a posteriori reasoning, and why he who has a why can bear any how.

item.title: House of Satoshi - Bitcoin und Friends – Bitcoin wird 18: Live-Podcast zum Whitepaper Day mit Niko Jilch, Serge Kaulitz, Adrian Fritz
item.description:
Bitcoin wird 18. Und 18 Prozent der Schweizer halten inzwischen Krypto, mehr als Deutsche und Österreicher Aktien halten. Volljährig also?


Zum zweiten Mal feiert House of Satoshi den Whitepaper Day gemeinsam mit der Luzerner Kantonalbank live im Kino.


***Auf der Bühne im Kino Koni Zürich***


  • Serge Kaulitz, Head DLT, Blockchain & Digital Assets bei der Luzerner Kantonalbank, der ersten Kantonalbank mit umfassendem Krypto-Angebot.
  • Adrian Fritz, Chief Investment Strategist bei 21Shares, einem der weltweit grössten Anbieter von Krypto-ETPs.
  • Und Niko Jilch, Finanzjournalist aus Wien und Host von «Was Bitcoin bringt», einem der reichweitenstärksten Bitcoin-Podcasts im deutschsprachigen Raum.


**Drei Sätze aus dem Gespräch**


Serge Kaulitz: «In Afrika schützt Bitcoin vor Inflation. In der Schweiz ist er eine Anlageklasse. Das ist nicht falsch, das bietet uns Möglichkeiten.»


Adrian Fritz: «98 Prozent aller Krypto-Assets sind kompletter Schrott. Das Schlimme ist, dass das die guten Sachen überschattet.»


Niko Jilch: «Selbstfahrendes Auto ist cool, aber selbstfahrendes Geld ist irgendwie unmöglich. Das ist schon eigenartig.»


**Darum geht's**

  • Bärenmarkt vorbei? Rino lässt den ganzen Saal aufstehen. Drei Experten sagen Ja.
  • Warum der Preis 50 Prozent fiel, aber die ETF-Bestände kaum, und was das über die Institutionellen verrät
  • Wieso ein Kantonalbanker «epische Diskussionen» führen musste, bevor seine Bank Bitcoin anbot
  • Coldcard: War das nur ein Produktfehler oder ein Treffer ins Herz von Bitcoin?
  • Zahlungsmittel oder Wertspeicher? Und warum Jilch findet, dass sich ein Fenster gerade schliesst
  • 30 bis 35 Schweizer Banken verkaufen Bitcoin. Wie viele haben ihn im eigenen Portfolio?


Krypto-Angebot der Luzerner Kantonalbank https://www.lukb.ch/private/anlegen/selbststaendig-anlegen/kryptowaehrungen?utm_source=houseofsatoshi&utm_medium=referral&utm_campaign=whitepaper-day-2026&utm_content=eventseite


Niko Jilch's Podcast: Was Bitcoin bringt https://www.youtube.com/c/WasBitcoinbringt


📬 Unser Newsletter: Bitcoin kompakt und verständlich: https://www.house-of-satoshi.ch/newsletter/




]]>

item.title: Thank God for Bitcoin – TGFB Episode 83: A Candid Conversation with Rapper and Truth-Teller, Zuby
item.description:
Zuby (@ZubyMusic) joins Jordan Bush for a wide-ranging conversation about faith, courage, and what it takes to be a positive voice in a divided world. He tells the story of his path from independent rapper to one of today's most recognizable social commentators, and how the COVID era pushed him to start speaking out. He also reflects on the upbringing that shaped his character.

From there, Zuby and Jordan dig into the ideologies shaping public discourse: gender norms, privilege, victim mentality, and the grievance culture that keeps people divided. Zuby makes the case for empowerment over resentment, for solutions over complaints, and for a sturdier definition of love and care. He closes by sharing how his faith has grown, why he worries about the UK's loss of national pride and purpose, and why he still believes optimism and individual responsibility can change things.

Rapper. Author. Speaker. Coach. Host @ZubyPodcast

'Strong Advice' book https://zubymusic.gumroad.com/l/zubyfitness

]]>

item.title: No Second Best - A Bitcoin Podcast – Did the Federal Reserve Just Open the Door to Bitcoin?
item.description:
Jamie Dimon just went on national television to push back against Bitcoin and crypto legislation. Hours later, a Bitcoin exchange gained direct access to the Federal Reserve's settlement rails.

At the same time, Morgan Stanley filed for a spot Bitcoin ETF while geopolitical tensions escalated in the Middle East and Bitcoin surged.

This episode breaks down the growing conflict between the traditional banking system and the emerging Bitcoin financial infrastructure, and why the global monetary system may already be bending toward neutral, hard money.

item.title: Bitcoin.com News Interviews – Amy Oldenburg on Morgan Stanley's Crypto Push, Bitcoin Allocations and AI Agents
item.description:
What happens when one of Wall Street's biggest banks goes all in on digital assets?


Amy Oldenburg, Head of Digital Asset Strategy at Morgan Stanley, joins Bitcoin.com News' Live News Desk at TOKEN2049 Singapore 2026. She explains how the bank passed $1 billion across its crypto ETPs in under six months, why some clients want an ETP while others insist on self-custody, and how its advisor models approach Bitcoin allocations.


She also explains why digital assets change the economics of hacking, what Morgan Stanley's new Digital Asset Lab is testing, and why she expects AI agents and digital assets to converge.

They discuss:

  • Why crypto hacks pay off instantly
  • Is Morgan Stanley already the everything app?
  • ETPs vs self-custody
  • How advisor models treat Bitcoin
  • The Digital Asset Lab
  • Tokenized assets beyond stocks and bonds
  • AI agents and the end of web browsers


A Bitcoin.com Live News Desk interview recorded at TOKEN2049 Singapore 2026. Not investment advice.

item.title: Bitcoin Audible – Chat_180 - Invalid Checksum: How I Almost Lost My Bitcoin Stack with STACKTOTHEFUTURE
item.description:
"There's a lot of emphasis on the moment at how AI is making everything less secure, and that is a part of the story. Of course, any tool, any powerful tool has its advantages and disadvantages or has the thing bad guys can use it, good guys can use it. But the power that I think this actually gives the individual for doing stuff like recovery, I think that in the long run, there's going to be way more people who use this to recover their funds than people who use it and manage to steal someone else's funds. Because of the information you can give it, I got it to interview me: how did I store the seed words? Did I do it in columns or did I do it in rows? Did I mix it? All that stuff I can choose selectively to give to the AI, whereas an attacker, they're basically going in with a kind of like a blank slate and trying to do an attack from relatively low amounts of knowledge in terms of your setup."

~ STACKTOTHEFUTURE

In this Chat, I sit down with my producer and good friend STACKTOTHEFUTURE to unpack how he almost lost half his Bitcoin stack to hardware wallet failures. First from the Coldcard entropy bug scare, then from a degraded Ledger screen and an “invalid checksum” seed.

We walk through his AI-assisted recovery process, why tools like BTCRecover and careful prompting can let you fix mistakes without trusting anyone with your keys, and how this led him to build Keybackup, an open-source printable paper backup for Bitcoin wallets.

Along the way we dive into AI as a net security positive, self-custody tradeoffs, wallet UX for normies, and the Opsec tradeoffs of being public about Bitcoin.

Guest Links

STACKTOTHEFUTURE on X (Link: https://twitter.com/stack2thefuture)

KeyBackup's Website (Link: https://keybackup.org/)

Chapters

(00:58:30) - Red-teaming code and the singularity stack

item.title: Bitcoin Audible – Chat_180 - Invalid Checksum: How I Almost Lost My Bitcoin Stack with STACKTOTHEFUTURE
item.description:
"There's a lot of emphasis on the moment at how AI is making everything less secure, and that is a part of the story. Of course, any tool, any powerful tool has its advantages and disadvantages or has the thing bad guys can use it, good guys can use it. But the power that I think this actually gives the individual for doing stuff like recovery, I think that in the long run, there's going to be way more people who use this to recover their funds than people who use it and manage to steal someone else's funds. Because of the information you can give it, I got it to interview me: how did I store the seed words? Did I do it in columns or did I do it in rows? Did I mix it? All that stuff I can choose selectively to give to the AI, whereas an attacker, they're basically going in with a kind of like a blank slate and trying to do an attack from relatively low amounts of knowledge in terms of your setup."

~ STACKTOTHEFUTURE

In this Chat, I sit down with my producer and good friend STACKTOTHEFUTURE to unpack how he almost lost half his Bitcoin stack to hardware wallet failures. First from the Coldcard entropy bug scare, then from a degraded Ledger screen and an “invalid checksum” seed.

We walk through his AI-assisted recovery process, why tools like BTCRecover and careful prompting can let you fix mistakes without trusting anyone with your keys, and how this led him to build Keybackup, an open-source printable paper backup for Bitcoin wallets.

Along the way we dive into AI as a net security positive, self-custody tradeoffs, wallet UX for normies, and the Opsec tradeoffs of being public about Bitcoin.

Guest Links

STACKTOTHEFUTURE on X (Link: https://twitter.com/stack2thefuture)

KeyBackup's Website (Link: https://keybackup.org/)

Chapters

(00:00:00) - Introduction

(00:03:42) - Pearcast and AI workflow

(00:06:47) - STACKTOTHEFUTURE joins the show

(00:12:12) - Coldcard vulnerability and Ledger screen fail

(00:20:47) - More supply chain attacks and fake wallet apps

(00:36:00) - Invalid checksum & AI-assisted recovery

(00:58:30) - Red-teaming code and the singularity stack

(01:30:35) - Upgrading paper seed backups with keybackup

(01:42:58) - Opsec, physical security, and PO boxes

item.title: Coffee with Noma - The top 3 Bitcoin stories of the last 24 hours, in about 5 minutes. Your Bitcoin – #14 · Nov 4, 2026 · Bitcoin Rage Quitting: A Bottom Signal? Midterms and Mercado Bitcoin
item.description:
Coffee with Noma #14 · Wednesday, November 4, 2026

The three biggest stories of the last 24 hours, explained simply.


#3 Mercado Bitcoin now says $36.3M was taken and $12.9M is already blocked. The platform is still paused.

#2 America voted. The AP says Democrats won the Senate; NBC and CBS project the House. In Ohio, Sherrod Brown won despite heavy crypto spending against him. Bitcoin dipped to about $75.7K and bounced back toward $78K.

#1 Rage quitting: holders are selling at a loss for the longest stretch since mid-August, and the Fear & Greed Index fell to 27. Why that has often come near a bottom, and why it's history, not a promise.


Question for you: have you ever rage quit an investment?

Not financial advice. Not sponsored.

item.title: The Bitcoin Frontier – Inside Wall Street’s bitcoin playbook with Denny Galindo
item.description:
Denny is a wealth manager and bitcoin research lead at Morgan Stanley, where he bridges traditional finance and bitcoin for high-net-worth investors. He operates inside one of the world’s largest financial institutions while developing frameworks to help advisors understand and allocate to bitcoin.

In this episode, Denny joins The Bitcoin Frontier to share how investors should think about bitcoin in a portfolio, the three core investor buckets driving adoption, and his thoughts on determining whether you’re underweight or overweight bitcoin. We dig into bitcoin’s market cycles and seasonal framework, the role of global money supply in driving returns, and practical strategies for gaining exposure in a volatile asset.

item.title: POD256 | Bitcoin Mining, Freedom Tech, and Awesome Tangents – 131. Hack or Be Hacked: AI, Linux, Binance, and the New Security Reality
item.description:
In this episode, we unpacked the growing wave of security failures showing up everywhere at once—from a severe Linux kernel vulnerability and the Binance hack to hardware wallet flaws, exposed IoT systems, and the broader reality that more critical infrastructure is now connected, fragile, and increasingly attackable. We talked through what these incidents have in common: the human element, weak incentive structures, and the fact that AI-assisted discovery is accelerating how quickly bugs are found and weaponized. Along the way, we debated open source versus closed source, why obscurity is not a real defense, and why self-custody and self-hosting still matter—even if they come with serious responsibility.

We also spent time on what this means for Bitcoin and mining specifically: why open source remains essential in Bitcoin hardware and software, how products like Heatbit’s BitWater and BitAir point toward a more accessible future for home mining, and why the current proprietary mining ecosystem still needs to be challenged and rebuilt. We wrapped with thoughts on upcoming threats, the risks posed by internet-connected devices and industrial systems, and a reminder that in a world where everything seems increasingly exploitable, vigilance, verification, and reducing trust assumptions matter more than ever.

]]>

item.title: Epicenter - Learn about Crypto, Blockchain, Ethereum, Bitcoin and Distributed Technologies – The DAO Security Fund: Turning a Historic Hack into Ethereum's Future | Griff Green
item.description:
Ten years after The DAO hack changed Ethereum forever, Griff Green returns to Epicenter to discuss the next chapter: the DAO Security Fund.


As a co-initiator of The DAO, Griff shares the untold story of recovering funds after the hack, why over 75,000 ETH remained untouched for years, and how its staking yield is now funding public goods for Ethereum security. The conversation also explores a provocative idea: Ethereum is incredibly secure—but still not safe for everyday users.


Topics covered:

1. The inside story of The DAO and its recovery

2. Why the DAO hack may be the only hack where everyone made money

3. The DAO Security Fund and funding Ethereum security

4. Quadratic funding, grants & public goods

5. Why phishing and UX remain Ethereum's biggest weakness

6. Can Ethereum become safer than traditional banks?

7. The future of safer wallets, OpSec, and the Ethereum Economic Zone


If you enjoyed the episode, don't forget to subscribe for more conversations with the builders, founders and investors shaping the future of crypto.

item.title: Bitcoin für Frauen – Folge 9 – Totgesagt, verboten, kritisiert: Warum Bitcoin trotzdem weiterläuft
item.description:
Bitcoin verbraucht zu viel Strom. Bitcoin funktioniert nicht bei Strom- oder Internetausfall. Bitcoin wird von Kriminellen genutzt. Regierungen können es verbieten. Banken wollten lange nichts davon wissen.

Solche Aussagen begleiten Bitcoin seit Jahren.

In dieser Folge schauen wir uns deshalb an, was hinter diesen Kritikpunkten tatsächlich steckt.

Wir sprechen über den Energieverbrauch von Bitcoin und darüber, warum Proof of Work überhaupt Strom benötigt. Wir schauen uns an, was bei Strom- oder Internetausfällen passiert und warum solche Abhängigkeiten nicht nur Bitcoin, sondern unsere gesamte digitale Finanzwelt betreffen.

Außerdem geht es um das Mining-Verbot in China und darum, wie sich das Bitcoin-Netzwerk nach dem massiven Einbruch der weltweiten Rechenleistung wieder angepasst hat.

Wir sprechen auch über Kriminalität, über den Unterschied zwischen Bitcoin und gehackten Börsen und über die überraschende Entwicklung großer Banken und Vermögensverwalter, die Bitcoin früher teilweise massiv kritisiert haben und heute selbst Produkte rund um Bitcoin anbieten.

Und dann gibt es da noch die Geschichte mit der Kanalratte – ein ungewöhnlicher, aber ziemlich treffender Vergleich für die Widerstandsfähigkeit von Bitcoin.

Wie immer gilt: Dieser Podcast dient ausschließlich der Wissensvermittlung rund um Bitcoin und stellt keine Anlage- oder Finanzberatung dar. Bitte überprüft meine Aussagen selbst und bildet euch eure eigene Meinung.

]]>

item.title: 21talk – USA & Stablecoins: Der geheime Plan zur Rettung des Dollars
item.description:
In diesem 21talk sprechen Daniel Winklhammer (CEO 21bitcoin) und Dino Heinert (21bitcoin) mit Markus Turm, Mitgründer des EINUNDZWANZIG-Podcasts. Im Mittelpunkt steht die geopolitische Tragweite von Stablecoins: Wie die USA über digitale Dollar ihre globale Währungsmacht sichern, welche Rolle Tether spielt und wie Europa mit Regulierungen wie MiCA darauf reagiert. Die Runde beleuchtet das Spannungsfeld zwischen BRICS, US-Geopolitik und staatlichen Überwachungstendenzen.Anschließend widmet sich das Gespräch den Herausforderungen im Alltag auf dem Bitcoin-Standard, der Bedeutung von Privatsphäre und Non-Custodial-Lösungen sowie den aktuellen Debatten um Bitcoin-Steuern in Deutschland und Österreich. Markus teilt persönliche Erfahrungen aus der Einundzwanzig-Community und gibt spannende Einblicke in die Entwicklung von Nostr-Apps, Open-Source-Tools und den Einfluss von künstlicher Intelligenz auf Bildung und individuelle Freiheit.EINUNDZWANZIG: https://einundzwanzig.space/


(00:00) Intro (00:46) Regulierung, Steuern & Schwarzmärkte (02:16) EU-Überwachung & Privatsphäre (GrapheneOS, Signal) (03:00) Privatsphäre & Peer-to-Peer-Handel im Bärenmarkt (04:09) Komplexität reduzieren: Nostr & Tippspiel Kickstr (06:43) Bitcoin für Anfänger: Barrieren & Onboarding (08:58) Fokus & Zielgruppe des 21-Podcasts (11:15) Non-Custodial vs. Broker & Börsen (12:53) Markus' kuriose Bahn-Anreise & Zug-Begegnung (18:58) Leben auf Bitcoin: Alltag, Akzeptanz & Lightning (22:52) No-KYC Lending & globale Stablecoin-Nutzung (26:00) Stablecoins in Österreich & EU-Regulierung (MiCA) (27:47) Das Geschäftsmodell von Tether & neue Stablecoin-Konsortien (29:28) Geopolitik: Digitale Dollar-Macht vs. EU-Ansatz (37:00) Kritik an EU-Bürokratie & Zentralisierung (38:15) Diskussion um die Bitcoin-Steuerdebatte in Deutschland (40:02) Das Gleichnis vom chinesischen Bauern (42:10) Einschätzung zur politischen Lage & Haltefrist (46:22) Rückwirkende Besteuerung & Lehren aus Österreich (50:06) Zitadelle, Konferenzen & Community-Events (51:24) Neue 21-Projekte, Apps & Nostr-Entwicklung (53:18) KI-Tools in der Open-Source-Entwicklung (55:14) Philosophie von Markus: Freiheit & „Kein Zwang, keine Gewalt" (58:19) Ausblick auf KI & finanzielle Bildung (01:00:20) Outro


]]>

Dr Bitcoin - The Man Who Wasn't Satoshi Nakamoto – The Last Podcast
item.description:
Mark and Arthur sign off from their five-year Craig Wright odyssey with a review of the third and final book in the Faketoshi series, which sees Wright embark on a series of epically fraudulent lawsuits, where his decade-long plan to be anointed Satoshi Nakamoto finally unwinds.


Volume 3 is available from faketoshi.co.uk in hardback, paperback, eBook and audiobook forms.


'Craig Wright is Not Satoshi' written and performed by Jonathan Mann.

item.title: The Peter McCormack Show – #227 - Gideon Rachman - How World War 3 Could Start by Accident
item.description:
Why does the world feel more dangerous at a time of extraordinary technological progress? Gideon Rachman joins me to discuss his book, War Is Interested in You, and the return of leaders driven by territory, personal glory and their place in history. We explore Putin’s ambitions in Ukraine, the pressures on NATO, Trump’s decisions over Iran and how miscalculation could turn regional conflicts into something much bigger.


Gideon explains why the risk of a wider war has risen, while arguing that World War III is neither inevitable nor highly likely. We also discuss nuclear deterrence, the cost of conflict for ordinary people, Britain’s weak growth, rising taxes and debt and what AI could mean for jobs and the next generation.

item.title: VERIFIED by Bitcoin Suisse – He Co-Wrote the Paper Behind Modern AI. Then Built NEAR
item.description:
His grandparents' life savings ended up in a Soviet bank book that became worthless. As a kid in Ukraine, he watched bread prices rise exponentially. Years later he co-authored the paper behind modern AI, and he's convinced AI and crypto belong together. 

Illia Polosukhin, co-author of "Attention Is All You Need" and co-founder of NEAR, joins Bitcoin Suisse to explain how the transformer actually works, why he left Google to start NEAR as an AI company in 2017, and why he thinks we've done almost nothing to prepare our systems for a post-AGI world.

item.title: 21Focus - Der Bitcoin-Unternehmer Podcast – Aus der Banken IT in die Welt von Bitcoin - Harald Betz
item.description:
Folge #61 – Ein Gespräch über Banken IT und Bitcoin Bücher

Harald Beetz ist seit fast 20 Jahren selbstständig in der Beratung für Banken und Rechenzentren. Angefangen als Banklehrling bei der Sparkasse, hat er früh den Wandel von Beratung hin zu reinem Vertrieb erlebt und sich auf IT-Projekte spezialisiert. In diesem Gespräch erzählt er, wie er von der Banken IT zu Bitcoin kam, warum er mit seiner Frau einen Roman über Geld schrieb und wie er sich heute zwischen Beratung und Content rund um Bitcoin positioniert.


Du erfährst,

  • wie Harald die Bankenwelt von innen erlebt hat,
  • welche Herausforderungen und Chancen es als IT-Berater gibt,
  • warum er Bitcoin zunächst wieder verkaufte und später mit völlig anderem Blick neu entdeckte,
  • wie aus einer Buchidee seiner Frau ein gemeinsames Projekt wurde
  • und welche unternehmerischen Lektionen er aus fast zwei Jahrzehnten Selbstständigkeit mitnimmt.


Kapitel:

  • 00:00 Begrüßung und Vorstellung
  • 02:15 Vom Banklehrling zum IT-Berater
  • 07:40 Veränderungen in der Bankenwelt seit den 2000er Jahren
  • 15:10 Einstieg in die Selbstständigkeit und erste Projekte
  • 22:05 Gescheiterte Produktidee und der Wechsel zur Beratung
  • 29:15 Erster Kontakt mit Bitcoin und die zweite Begegnung
  • 36:50 Der Roman über Geld und Bitcoin
  • 44:20 Zukunft der Beratung im Banken- und Bitcoin-Umfeld
  • 49:00 Wichtigste Tipps für Vertrieb und Resilienz


Links:

Youtube: youtube.com/@MiesesGeld

Webseite: miesesgeld.de

LinkedIn: linkedin.com/in/haraldbetz


---

Hallo, mein Name ist Daniel Wingen und ich suche den Austausch mit anderen Unternehmern die in Bitcoin eine wichtiges Werkzeug für ihr Unternehmen sehen. Ich möchte selbst lernen und andere dazu inspirieren sich mit Bitcoin im eigenen Unternehmen zu beschäftigen.

item.title: The Bitcoin Boomers – Don’t Use Ledger.
item.description:
Someone put a chip inside the hardware wallet. Then they waited. George Bodine walks through the Ledger reseller attack, the 2020 breach Ledger said hit about 10,000 customers (the leaked database had 272,000 names and home addresses), and why he's been throwing Ledgers in the trash for years. Bob Burnett explains the part everyone gets wrong: Bitcoin didn't fail, the things you plug into it did. Larry Lepard on 1933, phishing, the deepfake phone call he's waiting for, and why he wipes his Trezor after every use.

Then Bob previews something he's been building: a way to send a transaction that the world can't see until it's already in a block.

CHAPTERS

00:00 welcome, and a toast to the one kid who listened

00:43 a maxi with bitcoin in more than one bucket

02:28 the ledger reseller story

03:43 they waited

04:32 the 2020 breach, 10,000 vs 272,000

05:35 the fendi wallet

06:33 bob: bitcoin didn't fail, the interface did

07:57 two of three, geographically dispersed

09:22 the etf question

10:41 what if the government says it's illegal

11:25 opsec vs complexity

11:45 the coldcard entropy scare

13:09 why larry still runs single sig on a trezor

13:50 phishing, deepfakes, and the call from your kid

15:53 don't keep it in the house, wipe the device

17:58 bob's pre-announcement: replace by fee as an attack

22:10 private transaction submission

23:56 what to tell the golfing buddy with a million

26:17 self custody is not as easy as driving a car

27:41 let the hate mail come in

SPONSORS

Swan, Bitcoin only, recurring buys, withdraw to self custody. https://swan.com/boomers\

Sazmining, you own the rig, power at cost, coins go to your wallet. https://sazmining.com/boomers\

The Bitcoin Boomers is a panel for smart, successful people over 40 still on the outside of Bitcoin looking in. Plain English answers to the questions no one else will touch. Signal without the noise.

Your hosts:

Gary Leland, founder of BitBlockBoom

Lawrence Lepard, sound money fund manager and author of The Big Print.

Bob Burnett, mining entrepreneur and founder of Barefoot Mining.

George Bodine, the World's Most Interesting Bitcoiner.

Listen to the audio anywhere:

🍎 Apple: https://podcasts.apple.com/us/podcast/the-bitcoin-boomers/id1853058330\⚡ Fountain: https://fountain.fm/show/kHBRZl0Mb0MGWMELtjw4\

Subscribe: https://www.youtube.com/@BTCBoomers\

Follow the hosts:

Lawrence Lepard https://x.com/LawrenceLepard | Bob Burnett https://x.com/boomer_btc | George Bodine https://x.com/Jethroe111\

Follow the show: https://x.com/btc_boomers\

the opinions are the hosts' own. george's especially.

Nothing here is financial advice. Everyone's situation is different.

]]>

item.title: HashrateUp - A Bitcoin Mining Podcast – Hashprice Is Going to $80. Here’s Why.
item.description:
Is hashrate the next major commodity? Francisco Quadrio Monteiro (BD & Strategy at POW.RE) joins Jesse to break down how a Bitcoin hashrate OTC desk prices risk, who is buying hashrate today, and why hashprice could land around $70–80 within the next 12 months.


Since leaving Paraguay, POW.RE has shifted to trading physically delivered hashrate. Francisco explains why difficulty is now the only real risk factor in BTC-denominated contracts, why past data is a poor guide in today's market, and why Bitcoin treasury companies like Strategy should be deploying capital into mining.


TIMESTAMPS:

item.title: Bitcoin Rails | Isabel Foxen Duke – The Evolution of Privacy Technologies on Bitcoin | Seth For Privacy
item.description:
There are few people as close to the frontlines of Bitcoin privacy as Cake Wallet COO Seth for Privacy. After cutting his teeth building for Monero, Seth turned his focus to Bitcoin in 2022, with the view that making Bitcoin more private would ultimately help more people than focusing on a smaller niche target group alone.

“I would love for Monero not to need to exist,” says Seth, as we examine the technical hurdles of bringing true privacy to Bitcoin.

Although he believes that the ability to easily verify transactions on-chain is widely credited with helping Bitcoin gain early traction, Seth argues that its transparent design presents challenges that fundamentally challenge Bitcoin privacy, often making Bitcoin less private than the existing fiat system.

That said, Seth sees potential for key technical advancements in Bitcoin privacy — especially “Silent Payments,” developed by Ruben Somsen and Josie Baker — as having potential to move the needle on Bitcoin Privacy.

We dive into these developments and other key privacy technologies for Bitcoin in this episode, as well reviewing the regulatory and cultural hurdles faced by developers and users alike.

TIMESTAMPS:

🍰 01:15 The origins of Cake Wallet and early use for Monero before Bitcoin

⛏️ 07:22 How Monero's RandomX algorithm defends against ASIC-fueled centralization

🛡️ 15:15 The importance of default privacy and fungibility for blockchains

🕰️ 32:10 The early days of Bitcoin privacy: CoinJoin, Samurai, and Wasabi

🕵️ 39:47 Exploring the limitations of stealth addresses and BIP47

🤫 45:54 Silent Payments and friction with “handshake” transactions

🛠️ 55:00 Overcoming developer hurdles with Silent Payments

🪙 1:05:33 Managing UTXOs and the necessity of intuitive Coin Control

⛓️ 1:16:40 Evaluating Layer 2 privacy, covenants, and custody trade-offs

🔍 1:26:40 The core tension between supply auditability and privacy blinding

⚖️ 1:32:07 The chilling effect of the Samurai Wallet and Tornado Cash indictments

This interview is brought to you by:

LayerTwo Labs — developing research, software, and technologies for scaling Bitcoin via the integration of Drivechains (BIP 300/301)

Hashi on Sui Network — a primitive for executing Bitcoin DeFi transactions, without having to trust a federated bridge or other centralized entity

BitBox — an open-source Bitcoin-only hardware wallet, with smooth UX and no compromises on security. Check out Bitbox [dot] swiss and use code BITCOINRAILS to get a discount

]]>

item.title: Nerd Culture • A Gamekings Podcast – Nerd Culture #281 over Sir Patrick Stewart, Crystal Lake & Cyberpunk (Feat. Daan)
item.description:
Nerd Culture #281 is ook te bekijken via https://youtu.be/IndHpTB6rj0 

Het is tijd voor Nerd Culture #281! Deze week schuift speciale gast Daan aan bij Koos voor een aflevering die in het teken staat van een groot verlies: Sir Patrick Stewart is overleden. We staan stil bij de man die voor een hele generatie nerds Captain Jean-Luc Picard en Professor Charles Xavier was, en bij zijn opvallend grote rol in gaming. Ook nemen we afscheid van Eric Bauza, de stem van Bugs Bunny.

Daarnaast hebben we natuurlijk weer flink wat gekeken, waaronder Monster: The Lizzie Borden Story, de Friday the 13th-prequelserie Crystal Lake en het tweede seizoen van Cyberpunk 2077: Edgerunners. In het nieuws bespreken we de box office van Clayface, Wildwood en Klara and the Sun, de Elden Ring-film van A24, de nieuwe gameverfilmingen van PUBG en Mouthwashing en een nieuwe Alien-film van Ridley Scott. En we kijken naar de teaser van Death Stranding Isolations en de laatste trailer van Dune: Part Three. Genoeg te bespreken dus in deze nieuwe aflevering van Nerd Culture!

Eerbetoon aan Sir Patrick Stewart

Op woensdag 28 oktober overleed Sir Patrick Stewart op 86-jarige leeftijd in Los Angeles. Voor nerds wereldwijd blijft hij voor altijd Captain Jean-Luc Picard uit Star Trek: The Next Generation en Professor Charles Xavier uit de X-Men-films, maar hij was ook een gevierd Shakespeare-acteur die in 2010 tot ridder werd geslagen. Als gamers kennen we hem bovendien als keizer Uriel Septim VII in The Elder Scrolls IV: Oblivion en als Zobek in Castlevania: Lords of Shadow. In Nerd Culture #281 blikken Koos en Daan terug op zijn carrière en zijn iconische rollen. Zijn allerlaatste filmrol zien we in december in Avengers: Doomsday. Wat is jouw favoriete Patrick Stewart-moment?

Elden Ring wordt de duurste A24-film ooit

De verfilming van Elden Ring krijgt serieuze proporties. Het budget van de film van Alex Garland ligt tussen de 175 en 200 miljoen dollar, waarmee het de duurste A24-productie ooit wordt. Ter vergelijking: Marty Supreme, tot nu toe de duurste film van de studio, kostte rond de 70 miljoen. Kit Connor speelt de hoofdrol, Cailee Spaeny zit in de cast en George R.R. Martin, die meeschreef aan de achtergrond van de game, is producent. Het script zou minstens 180 pagina's tellen, wat richting een speelduur van drie uur wijst. De release staat gepland voor maart 2028, ook in IMAX. Weet Garland de duistere wereld van FromSoftware recht te doen, of wordt dit de zoveelste gameverfilming die struikelt?

Wil je adverteren bij de podcast Nerd Culture óf misschien bij een andere podcast van ILVY Network? Mail dan naar management@ilvy.com en/of kijk even op de website: https://ilvy.com/podcast

See omnystudio.com/listener for privacy information.

]]>

item.title: The DYOR Podcast - Blockchain, Bitcoin & Cryptocurrency – Crypto Security with Ruben Merre - DYOR 020
item.description:
How do you keep your cryptocurrency safe? You have to follow some crypto security best practices.

In this episode, we chat with Ruben Merre, CEO of NGRAVE, about how users can protect their funds. Ruben explains what can be done, why other hard wallets can be vulnerable and how NGRAVE Zero fixes that.

item.title: Bitcoin a blondýna – Bitcoin děti zajímá víc než daně nebo pojištění. Školy toho chtějí využít
item.description:
Jak zacházet s penězi se učíte doma, finanční gramotnost se dědí. Učí se o ní ale i ve škole, stejně jako o bitcoinu. Někteří žáci už ale vědí víc než učitelé.Více v dalším díle podcastu Bitcoin a blondýna. Tentokrát s Martinou Bacíkovou, která vede Institut ekonomického vzdělávání (INEV) a Pavlou Nýdrle, CEO společnosti Invity (SatoshiLabs), která je partnerem projektu Peníze a Bitcoin pod hlavičkou INEV.
